note: Drafted by Claude Code from official label / regulator pages. Pairs with NO DDInter record only. Only documented interactions; no entry ever says 'no interaction'. Enabled when status is 'reviewed' (a pharmacist returned the sheet) or 'author_checked' (prototype self-check by the project author against the official source; NOT a pharmacist review). 'draft_unreviewed' entries are ignored. Summaries are own-words paraphrases. Severity 'unclassified' = the source gives no severity.

entries.summary_en: The enalapril label names spironolactone as a medicine that can raise blood potassium a lot when taken with enalapril, so potassium should be checked often.
entries.source_section: Vasotec label, 7 Drug Interactions: Agents Increasing Serum Potassium (potassium-sparing diuretics)

supporting_sources.section: Aldactone label, 7.1 Drugs and Supplements Increasing Serum Potassium (ACE inhibitors and ARBs are listed as drugs that can raise potassium)

entries.selfcheck_comment: Vasotec label (enalapril) names spironolactone as an example of a potassium-sparing diuretic that can markedly raise serum potassium. Basis corrected from class to pair-specific.

evidence.section: Vasotec label, Drug Interactions: Agents Increasing Serum Potassium (names spironolactone); also Aldactone 7.1 lists ACE inhibitors: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22spironolactone%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22aldactone%22&limit=1
evidence.note: Enalapril label names spironolactone as raising potassium; spironolactone label lists ACE inhibitors the same way.

entries.summary_en_before_selfcheck: Both medicines can raise blood potassium, so taking them together can push potassium too high. This comes from a class-level statement in the source, so both drugs must be confirmed as members of that class.

entries.selfcheck_comment: Cozaar 7.1 warns about other drugs that raise serum potassium without naming spironolactone. Class membership: the COZAAR label (Indications) calls losartan an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB); the Aldactone label 7.1 lists ARBs as drugs that can raise potassium. The Vasotec label names spironolactone as a potassium-raising diuretic.

entries.summary_en: The levofloxacin label says blood sugar can become too low or too high in people also taking a diabetes medicine, so it should be monitored closely; gliclazide is a diabetes tablet.
entries.selfcheck_comment: Levofloxacin 7.3 refers to any antidiabetic agent. Gliclazide is an oral blood-glucose-lowering drug (NHS gliclazide page; WHO ATC A10BB09, sulfonylureas). Old summary cited a glyburide example that 7.3 does not contain; rewritten. Severity left unclassified.

evidence.section: Levofloxacin tablets label, 7.3 Antidiabetic Agents; WHO ATC index A10BB09 gliclazide (Sulfonylureas): https://atcddd.fhi.no/atc_ddd_index/?code=A10BB09&showdescription=no
evidence.note: Levofloxacin label: blood sugar can go too low or too high with an antidiabetic agent; gliclazide is a diabetes tablet.

entries.summary_en_before_selfcheck: The levofloxacin label says blood sugar can swing too low or too high in people on diabetes tablets, so sugar should be checked more often (label example: glyburide, a sulfonylurea like gliclazide). This comes from a class-level statement in the source, so both drugs must be confirmed as members of that class.

entries.summary_en: The ciprofloxacin label warns of low blood sugar, sometimes severe, when it is taken with diabetes tablets (mainly sulfonylureas); gliclazide is a sulfonylurea.
entries.source_section: Ciprofloxacin tablets label, 7 Drug Interactions, Table 11 (Oral antidiabetic drugs); 5.19 Blood Glucose Disturbances
entries.selfcheck_comment: Ciprofloxacin Table 11 names oral antidiabetic drugs, mainly sulfonylureas, for low blood sugar (sometimes severe). WHO ATC places gliclazide in A10BB sulfonylureas. Severity left unclassified.

evidence.section: Ciprofloxacin tablets label, 7 Drug Interactions (oral antidiabetic drugs, mainly sulfonylureas); 5.19 Blood Glucose Disturbances; WHO ATC index A10BB09: https://atcddd.fhi.no/atc_ddd_index/?code=A10BB09&showdescription=no
evidence.note: Ciprofloxacin label: low blood sugar, sometimes severe, with oral antidiabetic drugs mainly sulfonylureas; gliclazide is a sulfonylurea.

entries.summary_en_before_selfcheck: The ciprofloxacin label warns of low blood sugar, sometimes severe, with diabetes tablets such as sulfonylureas, so sugar should be monitored (gliclazide is a sulfonylurea). This comes from a class-level statement in the source, so both drugs must be confirmed as members of that class.

entries.selfcheck_comment: Verified against current product information, not only the 2014 annex: HPRA (Irish regulator) Motilium 10 mg leaflet (revised Sept 2022) tells people not to take it with levofloxacin among named antibiotics; the HPRA SmPC and EMA Annex III list levofloxacin under contraindicated QTc-prolonging medicines (4.3/4.5). The current UK SmPC (revised 04/11/2025, read on emc.medicines.org.uk, not a regulator domain) has the same wording. The source states contraindicated, so severity major.

evidence.section: HPRA Motilium 10 mg film-coated tablets leaflet, section 2 (do not take with ... levofloxacin); EMA Annex III SmPC 4.3/4.5: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/referral/domperidone-article-31-referral-annex-iii_en.pdf
evidence.note: Domperidone product information names levofloxacin among QT-prolonging antibiotics that must not be used together with it.
